html:
The Kichwa of the Pastaza River are an Amazonian Quechua speaking people of the lower Pastaza valley in Loreto, northern Peru, near the border with Ecuador.

Their Quechua spread into the Amazon lowlands in the colonial period, largely through missions and trade, and many river peoples adopted it. They live by fishing, hunting and farming along the river and its lakes. Since the 1970s oil fields in their region have polluted rivers, and Pastaza communities have protested and won agreements on clean up and compensation. Their neighbours include the Achuar and the Kichwa of Ecuador.
sum: The Kichwa of the Pastaza River are an Amazonian Quechua speaking people of the lower Pastaza valley in Loreto, northern Peru, near the border with Ecuador.
